about.head: About

intro.middle: came about after I read a
intro.end: about Portal, their developer platform built on Backstage. My first thought was: hold on, with a monorepo this big, I can actually build one for my own stuff. So I did.

about.lead: I'm Xifré Font, a senior frontend developer in Barcelona, and a lawyer in a previous life.

playground.detail: I wanted to see what a big monorepo really looks like: **Nx boundaries**, domain-driven design, **hexagonal adapters** for outside vendors like WordPress and the translation tool, and **a lint rule for every convention**, so nothing depends on someone remembering it.

tooling.detail: Then came the scripts, to speed up the work and the back-and-forth with AI. And the **decision records (ADRs)**, which I'm a bit proud of: every call has its reason written down, so nothing here is truly arbitrary. The tooling also **reports its own usage**. This way, an unused script gets cut instead of being mindlessly maintained.

workflows.detail: Building Huella Legal end to end taught me which steps come back on every project. I turned that into **workflow templates**, so the next rebuild, or the next site from scratch, starts from what already worked.

apps.detail: At some point it stopped being just a playground: it was good enough to grow **real apps** on. First **Huella Legal**, the law magazine I founded while studying, then Marina Roustan, and there are more to come.
